threads.body:
The per-chunk timing currently sent to `invocation._on_stream_chunk()` is a single timestamp taken after `next()`/`anext()` returns. Because `_on_stream_chunk()` computes deltas between successive timestamps (or start time), the `time_per_output_chunk` metric will include any caller time spent between iterations (time between the previous `yield` and the next `next()` call), not just the blocking read duration. This contradicts the PR description/#13 text that says timing is measured around the blocking `next()`/`anext()` call to avoid inflating metrics with user processing time.

Consider timing the blocking read itself (capture `t0` before calling `next()`/`anext()`, `t1` after it returns) and reporting the read duration (and TTFC as `t1 - start`) rather than inter-iteration timestamps.
